title: Drift Q-Learning
claim: Prior methods leave scattered, bridging or unsupported samples; ours concentrates sharply on the best supported modes.
layout: 2×5 grid of scatter plots, methods as columns, training steps as rows
description: A 2×5 grid of square scatter plots on a toy four-Gaussian bandit. Columns are Reward Reference, BCQ, Diffusion-QL, FQL and DriftQL, and the DriftQL title is orange. Rows are 5k and 100k training steps. The reference column shows four blobs in a cross, coloured on a white-to-dark-red reward scale. A colourbar from −4 to 5 sits below it. The right and bottom blobs are darkest, which marks the tied optima. In the other columns, light-gray blobs mark the data support and policy samples are overlaid. BCQ samples form a broad ring or ellipse that fills unsupported space. Diffusion-QL and FQL put dark points along a diagonal bridge between the two top modes, with scattered outliers. DriftQL's orange points sit tightly on the two high-reward modes, and the clustering is tighter at 100k. The eye goes first to the orange column.
caption: Value-guided mode selection on a four-Gaussian bandit with tied optima. We adapt the four- Gaussian bandit of Wang et al. [2023], arranging four isotropic data modes in a cross with the right and bottom modes tied for highest reward. Reward decays with distance from each mode center. The first column shows the reward reference, and gray blobs show dataset support. Rows show policy samples after 5k and 100k training steps. BCQ remains broad and assigns mass to unsupported regions, while Diffusion-QL and FQL move toward high-reward modes but retain scattered samples or bridges between modes. DriftQL concentrates on the two tied high-reward supported modes, with sharper mode selection by 100k steps.
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning requires improving a policy from fixed data while avoiding out-of-distribution actions with unreliable value estimates. Diffusion and flow policies handle this trade-off by modeling the behavior distribution to regularize the RL objective, but they require iterative denoising, solver integrations, and in more efficient variants, distillation or other approximations at inference. We propose DriftQL, which combines a drift-based behavioral regularizer with critic-driven policy improvement. The value signal biases the policy toward high-value regions of the data support, while attraction and repulsion together keep generated actions near the data and prevent collapse onto a single mode. DriftQL is implemented as a single network with a unified training objective and generates actions in a single forward pass. On D4RL and OGBench, DriftQL consistently outperforms diffusion and flow methods, advancing the state of the art. Under degraded data quality, where the baselines visibly struggle, DriftQL remains close to its clean-data performance, positioning it as a promising alternative to diffusion and flow-based methods while maintaining the simplicity and efficiency of deterministic approaches. Project page: https://driftql.github.io/
